He speaks English very fluent / although his native language / is completely different.
questions.solution_en:
The error is in the use of the adjective "fluent" in "He speaks English very fluent."

The verb "speaks" needs to be modified by an adverb, not an adjective. "Fluent" is an adjective, which describes a noun. The adverb form, "fluently," should be used to describe how he speaks.

Correct Sentence: He speaks English very fluently although his native language is completely different.

Hence, option (a) is the correct answer.

questions.q_en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.

She said to her brother, "Let me go to work."
options_en: She requested her brother to let me go to work.
She requested her brother to let her go to work.
She said to her brother to let her go to work.
She told her brother to let her go to work.
questions.solution_en:
"Let" when used as a request follows the following rules:

· "Said/said to" is changed to "requested".

· Inverted commas are removed and "to" is added.

· Pronouns are changed accordingly.

Example: The student said to the teacher, "Let me go home." (Direct Speech)

The student requested the teacher to let him go home. (Indirect Speech)

The following things in the sentence should change when changed from Direct speech to Indirect Speech:

Said to - requested

Let me - to let her

So, the sentence in indirect speech is: She requested her brother to let her go to work.

Hence, (b) is the correct answer.

· Option 3 ("grazed and some places is") has a subject-verb agreement error ("places is").

· Option 4 ("planted or") changes the meaning entirely.

Thus, the correct substitution is over-grazed and some areas should be.

Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. Proponents argue that it could eradicate poverty, improve public health outcomes, and provide a safety net in an era of increasing automation and job insecurity.

B. Critics, however, raise serious concerns about the immense financial cost of implementation, potential negative impacts on the incentive to work, and inflationary pressures on the economy.

D. Universal Basic Income, or UBI, is a theoretical governmental public program that has gained significant attention in recent policy debates across the globe.
questions.solution_en:

Sentence C follows up by defining precisely how "This system" functions, detailing the unconditional and regular payments to citizens. Sentence A then presents one side of the debate, outlining the arguments made by its "Proponents." Sentence B logically concludes the paragraph by presenting the opposing viewpoint, using the word "however" to introduce the concerns raised by "Critics," creating a balanced overview of the topic.

Hence, option (c) is the answer.

The chef cooked the meal perfectly, / but the new soup tasted / very bitterly to all the guests.
options_en: The chef cooked the meal perfectly
very bitterly to all the guests
questions.solution_en:

Such verbs are followed by an adjective that describes the quality of the subject, not an adverb. Here, 'bitterly' is an adverb modifying the action of tasting, which is incorrect. We need an adjective to describe the soup itself.

The correct word to use is the adjective 'bitter'.

Correct Sentence: The chef cooked the meal perfectly, but the new soup tasted very bitter to all the guests.

Hence, option (c) is the correct answer.

options_en: She said to me, "What is your favourite cuisine?"

questions.solution_en:
In the case of Interrogative sentences like this, "enquired (of)", "wanted to know", "asked", etc. in Indirect Speech is changed into "said/to" in Direct Speech.

In Direct speech, the verb is always placed before the subject, unlike in Indirect Speech.

For example:

The teacher asked him what his name was. (Indirect Speech)

The teacher said to him, "What is your name?" (Direct Speech)

The tense of the Indirect Speech is in the Past. So, the tense in the Direct Speech will be in the Present.

The following things in the sentence will change when changed from Indirect Speech to Direct Speech:

'Asked' changes to 'said to', 'my' changes to 'your' and 'was' changes to 'is'.

Hence, option (a) is the correct answer.

questions.q_en:
In the question given below, a sentence is given, divided into parts. One of the parts may contain an error. Identify the part that contains the error, and mark it as the answer.

The announcer (A)/ told to us (B)/ that a vehicle is (C)/ blocking the road (D).
questions.solution_en:
Part B has the error. The verb 'tell' and its form are followed by an indirect object (me, him, her, etc.) without 'to'.

The correct sentence is: The announcer told us that a vehicle is blocking the road.

Hence, the correct answer is option (d).

questions.q_en:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the underlined group of words.

The fireworks display was beautiful but lasted for a very short time before fading into the night sky.
questions.solution_en:
The underlined group of words, "lasted for a very short time", describes something that is short-lived and fleeting. The word "ephemeral" means "lasting for a very short time". Therefore, the one-word substitute for the underlined group of words is "ephemeral". Hence, (d) is the correct answer.
